result.summary: The Messenians, driven from Naupactus after Athens' defeat, scatter to Sicily and Libya, where dreams foretell their return. After Leuctra the Thebans recall them, and Epaminondas is guided by a vision and an ancient buried tin scroll of the Great Goddesses' mysteries to refound Messene.

scenes.title: Messenians exiled from Naupactus
scenes.summary: Messenian hostility to Sparta grows; they help Athens, then are driven from Naupactus and scatter to Sicily and Libya under Comon.
scenes.stakes: The Messenians risk losing their refuge and remaining homeless exiles.

scenes.title: Dreams foretell the return
scenes.summary: A priest of Hercules and Comon have dreams that foretell Messene's revival, and Leuctra brings the fated disaster to Sparta.
scenes.stakes: Comon's people hope to escape permanent exile.

scenes.title: Epaminondas' vision
scenes.summary: The Thebans recall the Messenians. Epaminondas, unsure where to build, is told in a vision to restore them.
scenes.stakes: Epaminondas must choose a site to check Sparta, and the Messenians must avoid unlucky places.

scenes.title: The bronze urn at Ithome
scenes.summary: Epiteles digs up a bronze urn holding a tin scroll of the Great Goddesses' mysteries, buried by Aristomenes. The dreamer was Caucon.
scenes.stakes: The lost sacred rites could stay buried and Messene unrefounded.

notable_quotes.reason: The oracle's closing line on fate, applied to both Messenia and Sparta.

analysis.text: Fate and reversal: Sparta's fall at Leuctra mirrors Messenia's earlier misfortune, and dreams and oracles guide the restoration.
The refounding of Messene in 369 BC by Thebes was meant to weaken Sparta by freeing the helots of Messenia.

language_notes.text: Sphacteria (425 BC): Spartan hoplites were trapped on this island off Pylos and surrendered to Athens, with Messenian help from Naupactus.
Ægos-potamoi (405 BC) was where Sparta destroyed the Athenian fleet, ending the Peloponnesian War in Sparta's favour.
Manticlus is a title of Hercules, said to recall Manticlus, founder of Messene on the Sicilian strait (Zancle). Zeus is the Greek form of Jove.
The oracle's line means misfortune takes its turn with every people; Messenian suffering would later be matched by Sparta's.
Castor and Pollux, the Dioscuri, were angered at the Messenians through the old quarrel at the Messenian-Spartan border, which led to war.
The 'old woman' in a brass coffin is a dream image for the buried urn; the riddling form hides what is to be found.
'Rolled up like a book' means a scroll, as ancient books were rolls, here of thin tin.

context_notes.text: Leuctra (371 BC): Thebes under Epaminondas crushed Sparta, ending Spartan dominance and making Messenian liberation possible.
Epaminondas was the Theban general and statesman who founded Messene in 369 BC to hem in Sparta.
The Great Goddesses are Demeter and Persephone, honoured in the mysteries at Andania. Aristomenes was the Messenian hero of the Second Messenian War.

literary_notes.text: The mother's death and return to life symbolizes the fatherland, Messene, dead and reborn.
Fate's reversal is ironic: Sparta, once the conqueror, suffers the same helpless doom it imposed on the Messenians.
The promise of fame beyond death hints at Epaminondas's glory and his coming death in battle.
